newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica commercial hub backs Cape Town Olympic bid.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica commercial hub backs Cape Town Olympic bid.

text.p: South Africa's commercial hub of Johannesburg and Gauteng province surrounding the city supports Cape Town's bid to host the Olympic Games in 2004, Gauteng Premier Tokyo Sexwale said on Tuesday.

"Gauteng supports the Western Cape and Johannesburg, the capital of Gauteng, supports Cape Town," Sexwale told a news conference 23 days before the host city for the 2004 games is announced in Lausanne, Switzerland.
"The black ring in the Olympic symbol represents Africa and I can tell you that Africa not only desires these games, but most importantly, it deserves them."
Nconde Balfour, the international relations manager for the Cape Town bid committee, said the technical aspect of the bid was secure and that it was time to exploit the emotional side.
Sexwale said the best way to do that was through President Nelson Mandela.
"The demonstrable effect of the Olympics would be to fulfil Mandela-ism. What better time than now, in his lifetime, to reward Nelson Mandela and his people.

"Cape Town was the first city to receive the president after his release from jail on Robben Island. While we were imprisoned there, the view of Table Mountain during the day and the lights of Cape Town at night gave us hope and helped to keep us alive."

Mandela will be present in Lausanne when the International Olympic Committee (IOC) delegates decide which city will host the 2004 games. The other four contenders are Rome, Stockholm, Athens and Buenos Aires.
The South African Broadcasting Corporation announced it would donate free air time on radio and television to promote the bid.
